model.name: Debt Instrument
model.purpose: Represent one governed debt instrument as the identity-bearing contractual definition of a debtor obligation and creditor claim, including economic terms, schedules, protections and change lineage without becoming a holding, payment, ledger entry, market observation or legal case.
model.scope_statement: Owns instrument and version identity; debt form and class; program, series and tranche context; contractual basis and governing-law references; issuer, borrower, obligor, creditor, lender, investor, trustee, agent and guarantor role bindings; currency, original principal or notional, authorized, issued and source-qualified outstanding amounts; issue, closing, effective, accrual-start, reset, due, exercise and maturity times; fixed, floating, zero, indexed and capitalizing rate terms; index, spread, cap, floor, compounding, day-count and business-day conventions; principal, interest and fee schedule formulas; amortization, bullet, sinking-fund, grace and capitalization rules; redemption, prepayment, call, put, conversion, exchange and extension terms; ranking, subordination, secured status, collateral, security-interest and guarantee references; covenants, conditions, waivers, cure, breach, default, acceleration and cross-default terms or external events; amendment, modification, restructuring, refinancing, novation and successor lineage; external issuance, holding, listing, trade, settlement, custody, valuation, rating, payment and default references; provenance, event and knowledge clocks, quality, access, retention, audit and loss-aware projections. Party, agreement, prospectus, issuance, holding, payment, ledger, market, valuation, rating, collateral, guarantee, benchmark, default, dispute, enforcement, insolvency, tax, filing and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Debt-instrument identity, version, class, contractual basis, participant roles and source-qualified legal and economic terms
Principal, currency, interest, schedule, optionality, ranking, credit support, covenant and instrument-owned lifecycle context
External position and outcome bindings, provenance, access, retention, validation and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning Party, Agreement, Prospectus, Issuance, Holding, Ownership, Payment, Ledger, Trade, Listing, Valuation, Rating, Collateral Asset, Security Interest, Guarantee, Benchmark, Default Case, Dispute, Enforcement, Insolvency, Tax, Filing or Record masters

Treating an instrument as a position, schedule as payment, original principal as current value, secured status as perfected collateral, covenant as compliance, rating as fact or amendment as derecognition
Autonomous contracting, issuance, amendment, trading, valuation, rating, waiver, acceleration, payment, enforcement, protected disclosure or record destruction

boundary_notes.distinction: Debt Instrument is a governed contractual aggregate. The candidate parent is marked for split and grants no inherited semantics or cascade authority.
An instrument defines fungible or bilateral debt terms; issuance creates supply and allocations, while positions bind holders, quantities and custody at time.
A contractual schedule is a formula or expectation. Amount due, cash transfer and accounting posting are separate records with their own event times and authority.
Observed or assessed values and opinions are external, source-qualified and time-bound; they do not rewrite the instrument's contractual terms.
The instrument owns referenced protection terms; assets, interests, valuations, compliance observations, breach findings, guarantees and default cases retain separate identity and authority.

boundary_notes.neighbor: CFI, FIGI, FIBO, ISO 20022 and XBRL
boundary_notes.distinction: Classifiers, ontologies, message formats and reporting taxonomies are versioned projections or alignments, not the universal storage interface or legal truth.

sources.title: IFRS 7 Financial Instruments: Disclosures

sources.relevance: Conceptual definitions for debt securities, positions, issues, valuation, coupon, principal, maturity and transactions.

sources.title: Introduction to BIS statistics
sources.relevance: Official scope and classification context for international and domestic debt-security statistics.

sources.title: Debt securities statistics
sources.relevance: Issuer, market, currency, maturity and amount dimensions used in security statistics, not a transaction system.

sources.title: ISO 6166 Financial services — International securities identification number
sources.relevance: ISIN identifier profile; an identifier does not establish ownership, validity or valuation.

sources.title: ISO 10962 Securities and related financial instruments — Classification of financial instruments
sources.relevance: CFI classification dimensions for financial instruments, with exact code-list maintenance kept external.

sources.title: ISO 4217 Currency Codes
sources.relevance: Currency identifiers for principal, interest, fees and observed amounts.

sources.title: ISO 17442 Legal entity identifier
sources.relevance: LEI profile for referenced legal entities; the instrument does not own legal-entity lifecycle.

sources.title: Financial Instrument Global Identifier
sources.relevance: Machine-readable identifier and instrument-class concepts; formal release is distinguished from beta development.

sources.title: Financial Industry Business Ontology
sources.relevance: Modular financial-domain ontology and release context for semantic alignment.

sources.title: FIBO Debt Instruments
sources.relevance: Debt-instrument concepts, terms, obligor and repayment semantics; latest development content requires an exact production pin for conformance.

sources.title: FIBO Bonds
sources.relevance: Bond, coupon, maturity and redemption concept alignment without making FIBO the storage format.

sources.title: FIBO Asset-backed Securities
sources.relevance: Pool, tranche and credit-support alignment while collateral assets and cash-flow observations remain external.

sources.title: ISO 20022 Message Definitions
sources.relevance: Versioned message projection context for securities, payments and reference data; transport messages do not own semantic identity.

sources.title: XBRL 2.1
sources.relevance: Reporting taxonomy, fact, context and unit projection context with explicit taxonomy-version and semantic-loss controls.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Unambiguous event, effective, observation and knowledge timestamps with seconds and explicit offset.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Attribution, derivation, revision, invalidation and delegation for terms, events, assertions and artifacts.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Quality observations, measurements, annotations and policies for source-qualified debt data.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Permissions, prohibitions, duties and constraints for protected instrument records and projections.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.relevance: Intervals, instants and temporal relations for accrual, reset, exercise and maturity schedules.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Controlled classification concepts, labels, schemes and mapping relations without collapsing unlike debt taxonomies.

sources.title: FIBO Production Release
sources.relevance: Distinguishes quarterly production releases from continuously published development content and constrains conformance claims.

Authoritative Party, Agreement, Issuance, Holding, Payment, Ledger, Market, Valuation, Rating, Collateral, Guarantee, Benchmark, Default, Dispute, Insolvency, Filing and Records registries
Approved debt-class, currency, jurisdiction, identifier, calendar, day-count, access, retention and interoperability profiles
Instrument creation, amendment, disclosure, projection, archive and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint instrument, version, term, schedule, option, covenant, role, relation, lifecycle and projection IDs; preserve every external master identifier and classifier edition.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative instrument identifier and namespace, exact version or terms head and source authority, never by issuer, name, amount or maturity alone.
Keep the instrument, issuance, position, scheduled cashflow, payment, posting, observation and legal case as independently canonical records.
patch_rules: Extensions declare debt class, jurisdiction, legal basis, role, amount, rate, schedule, option, ranking, security, covenant, lifecycle, access and interoperability effects.
Executed or published versions are immutable; amendments create linked successors with reason, authority, effective time and downstream impact.
Never silently change identity, obligor, currency, principal, rate, schedule, priority, collateral, covenant, source, access or external master reference.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when identity, legal basis, essential terms, source, event and effective times, authority, access and provenance survive.
Every ISO, FIGI, FIBO, XBRL, API, document or RDF projection pins versions and declares loss in identity, terms, schedule, role, lifecycle, authority and state semantics.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier from the issuer, borrower, registrar, depository, lender, trustee or regulator, qualified by namespace and record kind.
Governed globally resolvable instrument or artifact IRI.
Dimension UUID or ULID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish issue, closing, effective, accrual-start, reset, observation, due, exercise, settlement, payment, amendment, maturity, default, ingestion and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, instrument and version IDs, source authority, contractual basis, party role, amount and currency profile, event and knowledge times, confidentiality, retention and provenance.

policies: This model owns the debt instrument's identity, contractual terms, schedules, options, covenant terms and change lineage, not party, agreement, issuance, holding, payment, ledger, market, valuation, rating, collateral, guarantee, benchmark, default, dispute, enforcement, insolvency, filing or records masters.
Instrument definition, issuance, holding, scheduled cashflow, obligation due, actual payment, accounting posting and observation remain distinct.
Original principal, issued amount, outstanding principal, carrying amount, fair value, market price and recovered amount remain separately typed, sourced and timed.
Secured status does not prove collateral identity, current value, perfection or priority; a covenant term does not prove compliance, breach or default.
Agents cannot autonomously issue, amend, trade, value, rate, accelerate, waive, pay, enforce, disclose protected data or destroy records without explicit delegated authority.

read: Resolve instrument, versions, basis, roles, principal, rate, schedule, options, ranking, security, covenants, external outcomes, lifecycle, access and mapping loss.
create: Bind authoritative namespace, debt class, legal basis, issuer or borrower and initial sourced terms before minting an instrument.
update: Append successor terms, schedules, external references and lifecycle events with reason, authority, event, effective and knowledge times.
delete: Apply contractual, legal, accounting, regulator, privacy, audit, legal-hold and Dimension retention policy; tombstone only the catalogue view and never cascade deletion to external masters.

roles.name: Issuer, borrower or obligor
responsibilities: Own or authorize sourced obligation terms and changes through the applicable master system and legal basis.

roles.name: Creditor, lender, investor or holder
responsibilities: Maintain externally mastered rights and positions without changing the instrument definition.

roles.name: Trustee, registrar, paying, calculation or facility agent
responsibilities: Perform delegated administration and publish source-qualified schedules, notices or observations.

roles.name: Treasury, legal, accounting, risk and compliance steward
responsibilities: Review classification, authority, terms, accounting boundaries, risk disclosures and jurisdictional constraints.

roles.name: Data, privacy, security and records steward
responsibilities: Maintain identifiers, provenance, quality, access, legal hold, retention, audit and safe projections.

roles.name: Regulator, court, insolvency officer or other authority
responsibilities: Issue separately mastered filings, rulings or case outcomes without becoming the instrument owner.

access.default_rule: Deny by default for non-public contractual, counterparty, pricing, collateral, covenant, credit, dispute and personal data; expose only purpose-limited minimum projections to authorized roles.
exceptions: Statutory, regulator, court, insolvency, risk, audit and emergency uses require explicit authority, purpose, scope, minimization, time limit and audit trail.
audit_requirements: Record actor, represented party, purpose, authority, fields, source and target, result, event time, knowledge time, policy version and correlation ID for every read, write, projection, disclosure, denial and retention action.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension AGENTS.md and owner policies.

Instrument-class, jurisdiction, valuation, accounting, licensing, implementation-conformance and independent-review questions remain deferred.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
WM-ECO-037 EXTEND WM-ECO-005 is a candidate relation against a category marked for split, not an approved inheritance edge.
Loans, sovereign, municipal, corporate, covered, structured, securitized, Islamic, convertible, sustainability-linked and distressed debt require separate profiles.
IFRS standard detail is licensed and jurisdictional adoption varies; no accounting conclusion or full IFRS conformance is claimed.
FIBO master/latest pages are development artifacts; production release pins and licenses are required before implementation conformance.
conflicts: Instrument, issuance, position, scheduled cashflow, obligation due, actual payment, accounting posting and market observation are not interchangeable.
Original, authorized, issued and outstanding principal and carrying amount, fair value, market price and recovery may legitimately differ.
Secured status, collateral identity, current collateral value, perfection and legal priority require different sources and authorities.
Covenant term, compliance observation, waiver, breach, acceleration and legal default decision carry different authority.
regional_assumptions: Debt formation, enforceability, disclosure, tax, insolvency, consumer protection, benchmark, security interest, limitation and remedy depend on jurisdiction and instrument class.
IFRS, statistical, identifier, ontology and messaging sources serve different purposes and do not override the contract or applicable law.
CFI, FIGI, FIBO, ISO 20022 and XBRL mappings require exact release, profile, licensing and conformance evidence.
adversarial_checks: Reject an instrument without stable identity, exact version, debt class, contractual basis, obligor role, currency, principal or notional and authoritative source.
Reject a holding, payment, posting, rating, valuation or default case represented as the instrument itself.
Reject scheduled cashflows represented as amounts paid or accounting balances without external source records.
Reject secured or senior status as proof of collateral value, perfection, enforceability or recovery priority.
Reject amendments that overwrite executed terms or erase predecessor, authority, effective time and affected schedule lineage.
Reject autonomous issuance, amendment, trade, valuation, rating, acceleration, waiver, payment, enforcement, disclosure or destruction outside delegated authority.
